subject: Multi-year rate stability & renewal protection — request / escalation
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna@medigrowth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Doshi <samir.d@medigrowth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 3-year rate stability & renewal protection for Redwood deployment

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the infra and observability features look like a great fit for our new predictive docs product. We have budget planning starting next week and procurement asked if Redwood can provide a multi-year commercial arrangement with two specific asks: a 36-month rate stability (price lock) and a cap on any annual uplift at 6% on list rates.

Two other asks from our side:
- Renewal protection clause: if either party proposes material changes at renewal, MediGrowth needs a 90-day mutual notice and an option to extend under current economic terms for one additional year.
- Inclusion of a defined SLA-backed escalation path in case of production regressions/latency spikes (we can share an SLO appendix).

We attached the SOW draft (MediGrowth_SOW_v3.pdf) and a brief summary of expected usage across years. Can you escalate this to pricing/finance/legal? If we can get an answer by Friday EDT, we can lock in approval for Q3 spend.

Appreciate it —
Jenna Park
Director, Commercial Programs
MediGrowth

Attachment: MediGrowth_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: 3-year rate stability & renewal protection for Redwood deployment

Folks, forwarding an urgent ask from MediGrowth — they want 36-month price lock + uplift cap 6% + renewal protection (90-day notice + one-year extension right). They are a mid-market account but high growth and likely to expand across three products in year 2.

Can pricing/finance/legal give a stance by EOD Thursday? Procurement wants to include terms in their internal approval packet. I attached their SOW and a quick price sensitivity workbook I started (redwood_multi-year-term_summary.xlsx).

Key consideration: we should protect against excessive margin erosion while staying competitive for a 3-year commit. Marissa, do you want to lead the commercial recommendation? Markus — need your input on uplift cap tolerance and amortization. Lauren — if we permit the extension right, what guardrails should legal require (notice windows, contract re-opener triggers, termination rights)?

Thanks —
Connor
Head of Deals, Mid-market
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_multi-year-term_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 3-year rate stability & renewal protection for Redwood deployment

Connor —

I ran a quick models pass with a few commercial levers:
- Proposed commercial term: 24 months firm price lock + optional third year at a pre-agreed uplift cap. Rationale: 36-month absolute lock is high risk for us given expected model/hardware cost shifts in years 2–3.
- Suggested uplift cap: 8% annual max on list rates in year 3 only (years 1–2 locked at current quoted rates).
- Renewal protection: 90-day mutual notice OK; include a customer right to extend under current economic terms for one 12-month term provided usage thresholds (>= 70% committed capacity) are met. This prevents customers from locking then dropping to tiny usage.
- Tradeoffs: We take a modest margin hit in year 2 to secure expansion risk; require a minimum ARR commitment and a 20% non-refundable initial deposit to cover onboarding and reserved capacity.

Recommend we present this as an approval ask with two decision levers for execs: 1) Approve the 24/option-year structure with 8% uplift cap; 2) If leadership wants the full 36-month lock, require a higher commitment (min 40% greater ARR) and reduce the uplift cap to max 6% but conditional on a forecasted pass-through clause for major hardware/energy cost shocks.

Happy to draft the bullet request for Joel/Finance.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 3-year rate stability & renewal protection for Redwood deployment

Team —

Finance input: baseline support for Marissa's recommended approach with these caveats:
1) Approve 24-month hard lock, optional 12-month extension with an 8% cap (as proposed). 36-month unconditional lock is only acceptable if MediGrowth agrees to a cost-pass-through carve-out for extraordinary hardware supply shocks (defined threshold: >15% YoY model inference runtime cost increase) and a minimum commit uplift of +40% ARR.
2) Require a contractual annual review clause tied to our cost indices and explicit upper bound triggers; any uplift applied must be documented and notified 120 days before renewal to give market/commercial time to react.
3) Approve a minimum committed spend (contractual) and a 20% onboarding deposit as Marissa suggested.

If leadership approves this structure, Finance will draft the margin protection language and the required cost-pass-through formula for legal to embed.

-Markus
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 3-year rate stability & renewal protection for Redwood deployment

All —

Legal has reviewed and can live with the 24-month firm + optional 12-month extension at an 8% cap, subject to the following drafted guardrails (I'll push redlines to the SOW/TS on Thursday):
- Renewal protection: include explicit "extension election" mechanics — customer must meet usage and payment thresholds (70% committed capacity and no material breach). Extension must be elected with 120 days' written notice to avoid surprise.
- Cost-pass-through carve-out: define "Extraordinary Cost Increase" as a >15% YoY increase in our third-party GPU hosting costs OR a materially enacted tariff/energy surcharge; any pass-through must be capped at 50% of the observed increase and accompanied by a cost breakdown report.
- Notification: if we intend to apply any uplift in the optional year, Redwood must notify 120 days before renewal and provide line-item cost evidence; customer retains right to terminate with 60 days' notice if uplift applied above 5% after notifications (commercial termination with wind-down SLA).
- Deposit and commit: 20% non-refundable onboarding deposit OK; ensure funds applied to first-year invoices.

I'll prepare a short exec approval memo (one page) summarizing these points for Joel and Legal Counsel. Once we have leadership sign-off, Connor — you can present this to MediGrowth procurement along with the redlined SOW.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
General Counsel
Redwood Inference
